name: Lucerne
tagline: A medieval wooden bridge, painted houses and a lake ringed by mountains, with Pilatus and Rigi an hour away by cog railway or boat.
highlight: Walking across the Chapel Bridge at sunset, with the Reuss river, the water tower and the snow-dusted Pilatus behind.
shortDescription: A postcard old town on Lake Lucerne, with the Chapel Bridge, the Lion Monument, Mount Pilatus, Rigi and paddle-steamer trips, ideal as a Swiss base.
metaDescription: A Lucerne travel guide: the Chapel Bridge, the Lion Monument, Mount Pilatus, Rigi, Lake Lucerne boats, the old town, where to stay, how to get there and a two-day plan.
knownFor: Chapel Bridge, Lake Lucerne, Pilatus, Rigi
goodFor: First-timers, lake cruises, easy mountain trips, photography

image.alt: The wooden Chapel Bridge and stone water tower crossing the Reuss river in Lucerne

intro: Lucerne is a compact city of about 85,000 people at the point where the Reuss river leaves Lake Lucerne, ringed by mountains. Its symbol is the Chapel Bridge, a covered wooden footbridge from the 14th century with painted panels and an octagonal stone water tower, which was rebuilt after a fire in 1993. The old town has painted facades, medieval walls and squares, and the whole centre can be walked in an afternoon.

The setting is what makes Lucerne special. Mount Pilatus, legendary as the home of dragons, and Rigi, the 'Queen of the Mountains', both rise from the lake, and both can be climbed by cog railway and cable car. Historic paddle steamers cross the lake to villages such as Vitznau and Weggis, and a day's excursion combines a boat, a mountain and a train ride.

Lucerne is also a place with culture. The Lion Monument, carved into a cliff in the 1820s, commemorates Swiss guards killed in Paris in 1792, the Swiss Museum of Transport is one of Europe's best, and the KKL concert hall hosts a major music festival each summer. It is about 45 minutes from Zurich, making it an easy first base.

whyVisit.intro: Lucerne is the classic Swiss postcard, and an easy base for mountains and lakes.

points.title: Central location

attractionsIntro: The old town is small, and the mountains are half-day excursions.

attractions.name: Chapel Bridge (Kapellbrücke)

image.alt: The covered wooden Chapel Bridge and its stone water tower

attractions.text: A covered wooden bridge with painted triangular panels of local history, and a water tower that once served as a prison.

attractions.name: Lion Monument (Löwendenkmal)

image.alt: The Lion Monument carved into a rock face in Lucerne

attractions.text: A dying lion carved into a sandstone cliff to honour the Swiss Guards who died defending the Tuileries in 1792.

attractions.name: Mount Pilatus

image.alt: Mount Pilatus rising above Lake Lucerne

attractions.text: A 2,132-metre mountain reached by the world's steepest cog railway from Alpnachstad, or by cable car from Kriens, with views and walks at the top.
attractions.tip: Make a loop: boat, train up, cable car down.

attractions.name: Rigi

image.alt: The grassy east slope of Rigi Kulm in central Switzerland

attractions.text: A 1,798-metre mountain with wide views and Europe's oldest mountain railway, opened in 1871.
attractions.tip: Go up on a clear morning.

attractions.name: Old Town and Spreuer Bridge
attractions.text: Painted houses, squares and a second wooden bridge with a Dance of Death painting cycle.

attractions.name: Swiss Museum of Transport
attractions.text: A big museum of trains, planes and cars, popular with families.

thingsToDoIntro: Lucerne combines a town, a lake and a mountain.

thingsToDo.title: Cruise Lake Lucerne
thingsToDo.text: Take a paddle steamer to Vitznau or Weggis.
thingsToDo.tip: Boats are included in the Swiss Travel Pass.

thingsToDo.title: Climb Pilatus
thingsToDo.text: Cog railway up and cable car down.

foodIntro: Lucerne's food is hearty and Swiss, with lake fish and pastries.

foods.name: Chögalipaschtete
foods.text: A local puff-pastry pie filled with meat in a cream sauce.

foods.name: Lake fish
foods.text: Perch and whitefish from Lake Lucerne.

accommodation.intro: Stay in the old town or by the lake, and save by staying outside the centre.

gettingThere.intro: Lucerne is a central rail hub.

options.text: About 45 minutes, with trains every 30 minutes.
About two hours on the scenic Luzern-Interlaken Express.

bestTime.headline: May–October
bestTime.summary: Lucerne is mild, with warm summers and cool, grey winters.

seasons.text: Christmas markets, and snow in the mountains.

bestTime.avoid: Foggy days in November and January, when the mountains are hidden.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you plan.
tips: Go up mountains in the morning, before clouds build.
Make a loop rather than returning the same way.
Use lake boats with a pass.
Book hotels early for the summer festival.
Visit the bridge early or late.
Bring a warm layer for the summits.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Lucerne?

faq.a: Yes. It is one of the most beautiful Swiss towns.
Pilatus is more dramatic. Rigi has broader views and a gentler feel.
